questions.question: How can you prevent a car from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This stops car drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: To avoid getting tired, ride no more than:

options.text: Two hours in a day.
Four hours in a day.
Six hours in a day.
10 hours in a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Six hours in a day.
questions.explanation: Limit yourself to about six hours of riding per day to avoid fatigue. Take regular breaks on long trips.

questions.question: If a car is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow to warn the other driver.
Speed up.
Pull over to the side of the road.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is tailgating you. The driver may not see upcoming hazards that require braking.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Never use a staggered formation.
Put inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Not use your mirrors.
Keep proper space between riders in the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep proper space between riders in the group.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors regularly. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Maintain safe space between all riders.

questions.question: When riding at night you should:

options.text: Increase your speed.
Follow closer to the vehicle ahead.
Use the headlights of other vehicles to see the road ahead.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of other vehicles to see the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so others see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, keep at least this much distance between you and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum four-second distance under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are worse.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks.
Cross at about a 45-degree angle.
Cross slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at about a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross at a 45-degree angle with a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly or at a shallow angle can catch your tire and throw you off balance.

questions.question: The best braking is done by:

options.text: Using the rear brake only.
Using the front brake only.
Using both brakes.
Using the rear brake while downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes fully to stop in a straight line without locking either wheel. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: Motorcycle headlights are usually:

options.text: More powerful than car headlights.
As powerful as car headlights.
Less powerful than car headlights.
Larger than car headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less powerful than car headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is especially important in areas where hazards are likely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular pre-ride inspections keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard ahead
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals that there is a hazard on the right side of the road. Hand signals help riders communicate when riding in groups.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: The left position
The center position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you far from opening car doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: What should you know about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They are a good substitute for a face shield.
They are a good substitute for goggles.
They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop
Left turn
Right turn
Backing up

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right. Hand signals can be used instead of or with turn signals.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they see you in their mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center part of the lane to be seen in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the center portion of the lane.
Move to the left portion of the lane.
Move to the right portion of the lane.
Do not worry about your lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane when being passed. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When going through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the same part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the left part of your lane the whole time.
Stay in the right part of your lane the whole time.
Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to move to a different part of your lane anytime. The best path through a curve may not match the shape of the road.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Avoid making sudden moves.
Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more slippery than other surfaces.

questions.question: If you are taking a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Try to take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold during the ride.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold during the ride.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day and take rest breaks at least every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine—they cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat on a motorcycle. Tire failure is usually noticed by a change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Ride in a single-file line.
The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm and extends their index finger, it means the group should form a single-file line.
